description.narrative: Christian Aid will implement the project over 6 months (layering with HEF-4months), from September 2024 to February 2025, in order to address both the immediate emergency needs as well as prepare and monitor the beneficiaries for the upcoming 2024/2025 agricultural season where a La-Nina another potential disaster has been predicted. This extended period is critical, as the project area is expected to experience multiple crises, including the ongoing impacts of La Niña projected to result in floods that will affect communities. The additional two (2) months will allow the project to fully support the beneficiaries during the longer lean season, which this year is starting as early as September to March of the following year due to widespread drought. The project will ensure reporting is done concurrently with the HEF report to ensure alignment with Code 2 reporting guidelines. Goal: To improve the resilience and well-being of 1890 drought-affected households in Bulilima and Mangwe districts. Objective 1 (WASH): To strengthen lifesaving multipurpose water access for 1050 drought-affected households through repair, and rehabilitation of 21 defective boreholes. Objective 2 (Livelihoods): To enhance the income generation options for 840 drought-affected households through training on farm and off-farm livelihood activities, including livestock emergency management, sustainable agricultural practices, and internal savings and lending groups. Intervention Logic: The project aims to improve the resilience and well-being of 1890 drought-affected households in the Bulilima and Mangwe districts through a two-pronged approach. The WASH component will strengthen lifesaving multipurpose water access by rapidly assessing, repairing, and rehabilitating 21 defective boreholes, providing access to safe and reliable water sources. The livelihoods component will enhance income generation options through training on farm and off-farm activities, including livestock emergency management, sustainable agriculture, and internal savings and lending groups, building the long-term adaptive capacity and economic resilience of the target population. By addressing both the immediate needs of food, water and long-term livelihood diversification, this integrated project design is expected to contribute significantly to improving coping. resilience, recovery and well-being of the drought-affected households in the two districts.
